title: C/379/2005 — Pooja Tex Prints P Ltd vs. Surat-i
text:
In The Customs, Excise & Service Tax Appellate Tribunal
West Zonal Bench At Ahmedabad
Misc. Application No C/ROM/10009/2017
Appeal No.C/379/2005-DB
M/s Pooja Tex Prints P. Ltd. Appellant
Vs
C.S.T. & S.T., Surat-i Respondent
Represented by:
For Appellant: Mr. Dhaval Shah (Advocate)
For Respondent: Mr. L. Patra (A.R.)
CORAM:
HON’BLE DR. D.M. MISRA, MEMBER (JUDICIAL)
HON’BLE Mr. Raju, MEMBER (TECHNICAL)
Date of Hearing/decision:12.02.2018
Misc Order No. M/ 10349/2018
Per: Dr. D.M. Misra
Heard both the sides
2. This application is filed seeking rectification of the mistake claimed
to be apparent on the face of the order dated 08.08.2016.
3. The Ld. Advocate for the appellant submits that this Tribunal has
based its opinion on the statement of the Director, which was retracted
later, and not other circumstances which resulted an error apparent on
the face of the order. It is his contention that the Director of the
Company at the earliest opportunity, retracted the statement, but it is
not appreciated by this Tribunal in its proper perspective, hence, the
conclusion arrived by this Tribunal is not correct.
4. Ld. AR for the Revenue, on the other hand has submitted that this
Tribunal in para 6 of the order has analysed the evidences on record
including the admission of Director before the Panchas and value of

2 | P age C/379/2005-DB
subsequent retraction. In his statement, the Director has categorically
admitted to the allegation of sale of imported of fabrics without payment
of duty against cash and the realization was used in the disbursement of
salary of workers. Besides, the Director has failed to provide the address
of Sh. Iqbal Bhai, the purchaser to whom the goods were sold. In these
circumstances the affidavit filed by the director after one year was not
considered by this Tribunal in appreciating the evidences. It is his
contention that re-assessment of the evidences again at this stage and
consequently revisit of the Order, would result into review of the said
order, a jurisdiction not vested with the Tribunal in view of the judgment
of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of CCE Bellapur vs RDC
Concrete(India) Pvt. Ltd. 2011 (270) ELT 625 (SC).
4. We find force in the contention of the Ld. AR for the Revenue. After
analyzing in detail the evidences on record, this Tribunal has recorded its
conclusion at para 6 of the order. To reassess the evidences, as
requested by the applicant through the present application, would result
into review of the order of this Tribunal, a jurisdiction not vested with the
Tribunal in view of the ratio laid down by Hon’ble Apex Court in RDC
Concrete(I) Pvt. Ltd.’s case (supra). In the result, MA(ROM) application
being devoid of merit, accordingly dismissed.
(Operative portion of the order pronounced in the open court)
(Mr. Raju) (Dr. D.M. Misra)
